title: 12.10 Joint Ventures – Core Principles of Strategic Marketing

facts.fact: Equity joint ventures between a Chinese company and a foreign partner require a minimum equity investment by the foreign partner of at least 33 to 70 percent of the equity, as of 2010.
facts.quote: As of 2010, equity joint ventures between a Chinese company and a foreign partner require a minimum equity investment by the foreign partner of at least 33 to 70 percent of the equity

facts.fact: There is no minimum investment set for the Chinese partner in equity joint ventures with a foreign partner, as of 2010.
facts.quote: but there’s no minimum investment set for the Chinese partner.

facts.fact: The Chinese government began allowing equity joint ventures in 1979, marking the beginning of the Open Door Policy.
facts.quote: The Chinese government began to allow equity joint ventures in 1979, which marked the beginning of the Open Door Policy

facts.fact: Prior to 1986, foreign companies could not wholly own a local subsidiary in China.
facts.quote: prior to 1986, foreign companies could not wholly own a local subsidiary.

facts.fact: Abdel Nour's Vitrac Egypt company reached $22 million in sales before being bought by the Swiss company Hero.
facts.quote: Abdel Nour’s company reached $22 million in sales and was the Egyptian jam-market leader before being bought by a larger Swiss company, Hero.

facts.fact: The Vitrac joint venture in Egypt continued for three years before the French company sold its shares to Abdel Nour.
facts.quote: The two companies’ joint venture continued for three years, until the French company sold its shares to Abdel Nour

facts.fact: Shanghai Automotive Industry (Group) Corporation planned to increase sales of its own vehicles tenfold to 300,000 in five years.
facts.quote: has pursued plans to increase sales of its own vehicles tenfold to 300,000 in five years
